Definition: from G1909 and G4649 (in the sense of G1983); a superintendent, i.e. Christian officer in genitive case charge of a (or the) church (literally or figuratively):--bishop, overseer.
BiblicalUsage: Episkopos is an overseer, a bishop — a superintendent of the flock. Take heed to the flock over which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God; a bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober; and ye are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.
TheologicalSignificance: Christ is the Bishop of our souls first, and the overseers serve under Him. I believe the bishop's office only makes sense that way: He oversees us, and those who oversee the flock answer to the Shepherd.
RelatedEvents: Paul's Farewell to the Ephesian Elders
